140: [edit] The time for the sounding of the shofar is day and not night. The proper time to do it starts at sunrise. If one sounded it from dawn on, they fulfill their obligation. If one heard some of the blasts before dawn and some after dawn, they did not fulfill their obligation. Rem"a: If the amount of sounding during the day [after dawn] is the minimum quantity, see 587:3.

[edit] If one heard the nine blasts over nine daylight hours, they fulfill their obligations, even if done by nine different men, with one doing a teki'a, one doing a teru'a, one doing a teki'a. There are those who say that this only holds if there is no shofar sounded between them done out of order.

[edit] If one heard the nine blasts from nine different men simultaneously, he does not fulfill his obligation, because there is no teki'a before and after everything. Rem"a: If two simultaneously blasted the whole order of blasts, and even if one sounded a horn, it is valid, because he will pay attention to the shofar (Hagahot Asheri and Gemara chapter "Ra'uhu Beit Din").
[edit] If one person needs to hear the initial teki'a and one person needs to hear the final teki'a, one teki'a can fulfill each of their obligations.

[edit] If Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbat, there are no shofar blasts. Rem"a: And it is forbidden to move the shofar unless one needs its form or spot (Or Zarua and Hagahot Asheri at the end of chapter "Bameh Madlikin").
